JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 02-02-2025 at about 3-00 p.m., the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 17-HA-7268 from his residence towards Grocery shop on Old Canara Bank main road and when he reached near Siramagondanahalli, Davanagere,
at that time the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-17-N-3896 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, petitioner was shifted to Chigateri District Hospital, Davanagere wherein admitted as an inpatient.
So far, the petitioner has spent huge amount towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 38 years.
The petitioner was working as Painter and earning sum of Rs.25,000/- pm.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 - the R.C. owner of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-17-N-3896 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed exparte.

5. The Respondent no.2/the insurer of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-17-N-3896 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
The respondent no.2 has contended that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding a valid driving license and said vehicle was not having valid FC at the time of accident.

It is further contended that the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner himself, who was not holding valid driving license and riding the vehicle without wearing helmet and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle.

6. Heard the arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.
Raghu N vs Nagaraj V on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143745010/
2 7.

Based on the pleadings, this tribunal framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained injuries on account of road traffic accident on 02-02-2025 at about 3-00 pm., on Old Canara Bank main road,
Siramagondanahalli, Davanagere, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-17-N-3896 ?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What order or Award ?
8. The petitioner got examined herself as Pw1 and two witnesses are examined as PW.2 and PW.3 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P17.
On the other, the respondent no.2 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.

9. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 02-02-2025 at about 3-00 p.m., when he was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-17-HA-7268 from his residence towards Grocery shop on Old Canara Bank main road and when he reached near Siramagondanahalli, Davanagere

, at that time the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-17-N-3896 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to his motorcycle, result of which, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 7 which are the police records such as F.I.R, Spot mahazar with Rough sketch, Seizure Mahazar, IMV report, Wound certificate, Charge sheet, etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Raghu .N, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.0050/2025 by Davanagere Rural Police Station for the offence punishable under section 281, 125(a) of BNS, 2023.
After completion of investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under section 281, 125(b) of BNS, 2023.

sentences.text: So far as the allegation made against the driver of the offending vehicle is concerned, according to the petitioner at the time of accident he was proceeding from Hadadi towards Davanagere and the offending vehicle which came from behind hit to the vehicle of the petitioner on its rear side.
If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 15 feet.
The accident in question has occurred on the left side of the said road.
When the offending vehicle was proceeding from behind the vehicle of the petitioner, driver of the offending vehicle ought to have maintained minimum distance between the two vehicles.
Had he maintained minimum distance, this accident could have been avoided.

Though the respondent no.2 who is the insurer of the offending vehicle has disputed the manner of accident, but no where has stated or posed suggestion to the PW.1 how according to them, accident in question has occurred.

The respondent no.1 who is the owner of the offending vehicle has remained absent and thereby not disputed either the involvement of offending vehicle or the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of his vehicle.
Even respondent no.2 also has not taken any steps to examine the driver of the offending vehicle and thereby not placed any rebuttal evidence to negative the contention taken by the petitioner.

Hence, by relying upon the unrebutted oral and documentary evidence it can be said that,
the driver of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident.
Hence, Issue no.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and discharge summary which are marked at Ex.P5 and Ex.P8.
On going through the medical documents it reveal that petitioner has taken treatment at Chigateri District Hospital, Davanagere as an inpatient from 02-02-2025 to 24-02-2025 for a period of 23 days.
As per wound certificate the petitioner has sustained one injury which is grievous in nature.

15. Dr. Avinash Parthasarathy - Orthopedic Surgeon at Sreenivasa Hospital, Bangalore is examined as PW.2 and through him OP slip, disability assessment proforma and x-rays are marked as Ex.P12 to Ex.P14.
PW.2 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 16-10-2025 for assessment of disability.
PW.2 further deposed that petitioner has difficulty in doing his routine physical activities.
PW.2 further deposed that petitioner has suffered permanent physical impairment in left lower limb at 50% and on whole body at 17%.
16. If the cross examination of PW.2 is perused, he has not given treatment to the petitioner at any point of time, except assessing the disability.
As per the evidence of PW.2 the fracture injury is united and implant is already removed.
Though the learned counsel for respondent no.2 has cross examined the PW.2, but there is no reason to disbelieve the evidence of PW.2.

The mere fact that,
PW.2 is not a treated doctor or that fracture injury is united and implant is removed the court cannot come to the conclusion that the petitioner has not suffered any physical disability.

Hence,
this court considers the physical disability suffered by the petitioner as 16% (ie) 1/3rd of the disability on particular limb.
17. Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken, this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.

sentences.text: Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained one grievous injury.

Hence taking into consideration the nature of injuries sustained, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.75,000/-
towards pain and suffering.
19. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, he has produced 12 medical bills for Rs.4,792/- as per Ex.P10.

Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.4,792/-.
20.
It is stated that petitioner was working as painter and earning sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
But to substantiate the said contention, Petitioner has not produced any materials.

Hence this court considering the age of petitioner, year of accident and the place of residence, considers the income of the Petitioner as Rs.17,000/- p.m.
21.
The petitioner has sustained one grievous injury and has taken treatment for 23 days as inpatient in Chigateri District Hospital, Davanagere.
Hence the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature, it is reasonable to hold that period of 03 months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking into consideration the avocation of petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation, this court takes the loss of income during the laid down period as Rs.17,000/- p.m., for 03 months.

Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.51,000/- (17,000 X 3)
towards loss of income during the laid down period.
22. From the evidence of PW.1 and as borne out by medical records, Petitioner has taken treatment at Chigateri District Hospital, Davanagere.
Further for 23 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
He has taken nourishment and needs further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.
Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.30,000/- taking into consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2025.
23. The petitioner has contended that, he was aged about 38 years as on the date of accident.
Ex.P7 is the Aadhar card of the petitioner, which shows his date of birth as 01-01-1984 that means he was aged about 41 years.

It is vehemently argued by the learned counsel for petitioner and even the petitioner in his evidence has deposed that, in the Aadhaar card his date of birth is wrongly mentioned as 01-01-1984, and his actual date of birth is 01-01-1986
, hence, prayed to consider his age as 38 years.
But, when the document produced by the petitioner himself discloses the age of the petitioner as 41 years, tribunal cannot accept the oral evidence of petitioner regarding his age.
Hence considering the copy of Aadhaar card, this court has taken the age of the petitioner as 41 years at the time of accident.

24. So taking into consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.17,000/- p.m and if 16% loss of earning capacity is considered and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 41 years, as per Sarla Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 41 to 45 is '14'.
So by applying the multiplier '14' the future loss of income due to disability comes to Rs.4,56,960/- (i.e., 17,000 x 12 x 14 x16% )-.

Hence this Tribunal Raghu N vs Nagaraj V on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143745010/
5 holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.4,56,960/- towards future loss of income due to disability.

sentences.text:
25. Thus the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No.
 1. Towards pain & sufferings Rs. 75,000-00  2. Medical expenses Rs. 4,792-00  3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 51,000-00  laid up period  4.
Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 30,000-00  charges and nourishing food
5. Loss of Future Income Rs. 4,56,960-00  Total Rs. 6,17,752-00
Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.6,17,752/-.
(Rupees Six Lakh Seventeen thousand Seven Hundred and Fifty Two only).
26. As regarding liability is concerned, respondent no.1 is the RC owner and respondent no.2 is the Insurer of the offending vehicle.
There is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.2 this tribunal directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered.
27. Issue No.3:
In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this Issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.6,17,752/- (Rupees Six Lakh Seventeen thousand Seven Hundred and Fifty Two only) with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
